Lighting reads the Filter's per-viewer decoy list, an object the Filter owns, not the block. This follows `architecture.md` § API Boundaries ("Filter and Debug only") and Principle 3 over the broader wording in the kernel GDD's CR-10 table. ADR-0024 owns only the shape of the Filter's query surface.
144	- Presentation never reads another presenter's private state. A presenter may call a getter on a **strictly earlier stage's** product (the camera pose, the beam pose, the decoy list). Each presenter declares `reads: Array[int]` of stage ids at registration and the driver's freeze check fails boot if any entry is not strictly less than the presenter's own stage. A visual presenter never reads the Audio presenter or any audio level, bus meter, cue or voice state (TR-audio-042); Audio is stage 8 and nothing reads from it.
145	- The simulation (`src/kernel/`, `src/sim/`) never names a presentation class, a `Node`-derived class, `CanvasItem`, `Camera2D` or `Viewport`. `zoom`, `k`, `k_auto` and `field_h` appear only under `src/presentation/` and the Pipeline root (TR-shipbody-044); a lint checks the identifiers.
146	- Presentation reads settings (reduced motion, reduce flashing) from the settings store; **no simulation callable reads a setting**, and no toggle writes a block. A test runs one command stream with each toggle on and off and compares the tick count and `state_hash` (TR-pxl-034).
147	- **Cosmetic randomness: presentation hashes use `Ihash` or `Ihash.h32` (ADR-0005 § 2.6) with a fixed non-zero per-system seed**, never the global RNG, never `RandomNumberGenerator`, and **never `DetRng.derive` (ADR-0005 bans it in presentation)**. PF-37's "no dependence on integer overflow" wording is waived for the `Ihash` family because 64-bit wrap is the pinned, golden-tested behaviour (TD-29); the Perception Filter's D.14 keeps its masked hash until ADR-0024 migrates it, and D.14's specific form is ADR-0024's. A truth-channel visual that must be reproducible (a trail) **reads `Ihash` keyed by `world_seed` (ADR-0005 § 2.6)** with a fixed per-system seed, because the simulation never draws the `trail.vis` value (TD-28); it writes nothing back.
148	
149	**Write allow-list (PRESENTATION and INPUT_SURFACE):** `CanvasItem` properties (including `position`, `visible`, `modulate`, `z_index`, `frame`, `flip_h`, `texture` and so on, with the placement rule of § 4), `Material` and shader parameters, `Light2D`, `LightOccluder2D` and `CanvasModulate` properties, particle properties, and audio-player and audio-bus properties through the Audio presenter. Never: a block, a command (outside § 7), a physics body, `Camera2D.*`, `Viewport.*`, `SubViewport.*`, `SubViewportContainer.*` or `CanvasLayer.*` members **outside the Pipeline root and the camera host** (PR-8 item 4 and its lint AC), `Engine.time_scale`, `SceneTree.paused` (pause is the control plane's `PauseGate`, ADR-0002), synthetic input (`Input.parse_input_event`, `Input.action_press`), and file I/O (Settings and the Save host have their own owners).
150	
151	**The Layout PROJECTOR never creates `Light2D` or `LightOccluder2D`** (TR-section-024); Lighting's occluder builder is also a PROJECTOR and is the one class that does. The declared-classes list at registration is what the lint compares. The PROJECTOR scene shape, the Y-sort key and `entity_id` namespaces belong to ADR-0034 (this ADR owns placement only).
152	
153	**Lighting's occluder builder is chunk-exempt inside a shadow light's reach (amended 2026-10-29, sync knock-on fix, round 3; 2d-lighting-and-occlusion.md LO-11).** The builder rebuilds a section that intersects an active shadow light's reach disc as a **single chunk, exempt from the `BUILD_TILES_PER_FRAME` slice**, and applies the resulting polygons to its pooled `LightOccluder2D` nodes in **one apply at the end of its last chunk**. Stage 0 (`PROJECT`) therefore completes that apply before the `LIGHTING` stage (6) of the same frame, so a lit frame never draws a half-updated occluder set ("light through a wall" cannot appear for an in-reach section). **Any other rebuild** (a section outside every active shadow light's reach, or an `ALL` rebuild across many sections) stays chunked: the old complete occluder set keeps drawing, nothing is applied piecemeal, and the frames until the final apply are counted as event frames (Lighting's LO-11 counter), not as a ceiling breach. The exemption belongs to the occluder builder only; the Layout projector and `body.projector` keep the `BUILD_TILES_PER_FRAME` slice.
154	
155	A presenter output signal that crosses into simulation does not exist: the flow is state, notification, presentation, and never the reverse (CR-10 "Sim never calls presentation").
156	
157	### 2. Dirty-mark-then-draw
158	
159	**The handler contract.** The kernel invokes each subscriber handler through a registered `Callable` with a reused `NotifyContext` (ADR-0003 § 3), exactly like every other kernel-invoked callable. The shape is ADR-0003's, as fixed by ADR-0004 § 2 (re-read 2026-10-28; it matches):
160	
161	```gdscript
162	func _on_changes(batch: ChangeBatch, ctx: NotifyContext) -> CompletionToken:
163		_dirty.absorb(batch)        # ADR-0004 DirtyAccumulator (capacity facet.key_capacity); allocates nothing; is_all on overflow
164		return ctx.complete()       # last statement; nothing follows it
165	```
166	
167	This replaces the architecture document's `-> void` example (§ GDD sync). A handler **must** do only this: copy the batch's keys into the presenter's pre-sized dirty structure, copy the scalar fields it needs from an event record into a fixed-size ring, and return. A handler **must never**: read a view, touch a node, create a `Callable` or a container, emit an engine signal, `await`, call `submit`, or write any property. A handler returns its `CompletionToken` synchronously, so `await` is banned **lexically** in any script registered through a `PresenterDescriptor` or that calls `.subscribe(` (ADR-0010 PRES rule, TD-16, with a bad fixture); the kernel's token-identity check is the runtime backstop and records anything other than the armed token, including a suspended coroutine state, as `INCOMPLETE` (ADR-0004 § 2), which counts against the handler. A handler fault is counted and never fatal (ADR-0003).
168	
169	**Why the handler does not draw.** It runs inside P5 with writes disabled and its cost is added to every other subscriber's; a catch-up frame already runs the tick loop up to four times (`MAX_TICKS_PER_FRAME`) and `INPUT_SURFACE` handlers run once per tick. Reading views there would also read a state that a later tick in the same frame is about to replace.
170	
171	**Delivery recap (properties this ADR relies on; ADR-0004 owns the mechanism):**
172	- PRESENTATION, PROJECTOR and DIAGNOSTIC batches arrive **once per rendered frame**, after the frame's last tick, one `ChangeBatch` per dirty block per subscription, with the union of the frame's keys (`is_all` true past `MAX_DIRTY_KEYS` 256; this text's "`ALL`" means `batch.is_all`). INPUT_SURFACE and REPLICATION get every tick's batch. A 0-tick frame delivers nothing.
173	- A restore delivers one `is_all` batch per block to every class when `LOADING` becomes `RUNNING`, with `batch.tick` set to the restored `T` (ADR-0004 P5/load delivery). **`ChangeBatch` carries no load marker, by design** (ADR-0004 § 6 states it; see `PresentationClock.load_seq`), so `is_all` is indistinguishable from a mass change; the restore edge is `load_seq` (§ 6).
174	- Notifications carry no state; event records (`BODY_TRANSFER`, `POD_ARRIVED`, `DERELICT_LOADED`) carry identifiers only.
175	
176	**The draw side.** Each presenter keeps two things, and its `present(frame)` early-outs only when both are empty:
177	- `dirty`: which blocks or keys changed since its last draw. Dirty drives **bulk and structural reads** (lists, queries, rebuilds, layout of plates): a presenter performs a bulk read of a block only when that block, or `ALL`, is dirty (TR-instr-005: derived inputs refresh once per Graph step because the Graph dirties its keys once per step, never per frame).
178	- `animating`: whether anything still moves on `tick_alpha` or `present_time` (an interpolated position, a needle ramp, a fade, flow scroll). **Interpolation needs a draw on frames with no notification**, because a 144 fps frame between two ticks has a new `tick_alpha` and no new state; the example in `architecture.md` that returns when `_dirty.is_empty()` would freeze motion on those frames and is corrected. Cheap scalar getters on the `interpolated` pair (previous and current position) may be read every frame while `animating`.
179	- `ALL` means "rebuild everything from the views, and draw the end state with no transition": the correct and sufficient response both to a restore and to a mass change. A presenter bounds a rebuild by its own budget (PROJECTOR: `BUILD_TILES_PER_FRAME`, chunked across frames, continuing to draw the last complete state until the chunks finish). One exception, stated in § 1 (amended 2026-10-29, sync knock-on fix, round 3): Lighting's occluder builder rebuilds a section intersecting an active shadow light's reach disc as one chunk outside the `BUILD_TILES_PER_FRAME` slice and applies its polygons to the pooled `LightOccluder2D` nodes in a single apply at the end of its last chunk, so stage 0 finishes before `LIGHTING` (stage 6) in the same frame; every other occluder rebuild keeps the old complete set drawing until the final apply, and the frames in between are counted event frames.
180	- Event records are copied into a fixed ring; ring overflow degrades to a full rebuild and counts `PRESENTER_EVENT_OVERFLOW`. Events are never dropped silently, and a `BODY_TRANSFER` is delivered to the camera as a rebase, not a cut (TR-shipbody-049; the rebase math is ADR-0008's).
181	
182	**Coherence by construction.** The driver runs inside `PipelineRoot._process` at `PRESENTATION` (0), after the TickDriver (-50) in the same `_process` pass, and the kernel cannot tick while presentation runs, so every presenter in a frame reads the same committed tick `T`. No presenter copies state to be consistent.
183	
184	**Latency, stated honestly.** Discrete committed state (a bead appears, a light toggles) is drawn in the same rendered frame as the P5 that announced it, with zero frames of delay (TR-assembly-045). Continuously interpolated motion lags the commit by up to one tick by construction, because `tick_alpha` is clamped at 1 and never extrapolates (PR-4 rule 3, PR-9 rate table).
185	
186	**A debug-build safety net, in addition to ADR-0004's check that every changed block marked a dirty key.** A presenter that applies **key-level incremental updates** (the PROJECTOR chunks, the Trail, Lighting's occluder builder) exposes `rebuild_signature() -> int` in debug and test builds only (a hash of its derived draw model). The dirty-correctness test (Validation) runs a scripted command stream through that incrementally updated presenter and a fresh presenter fed `ALL`, and requires equal signatures. A presenter that forgot to react to a key is caught by that test, not in play. A presenter that rebuilds a whole block whenever any of its keys is dirty is **exempt**, because the equivalence proves nothing for it. This is a story-level definition-of-done item for the presenter's story that references this ADR, not a blanket ADR requirement.
187	
188	### 3. One driver, one frame object, fixed named stages
189	
190	**`PipelineRoot` is the `PresentationHost`** (ruling TD-03; ADR-0008 owns the edit to its § 6.1, § 6.2 and § 7.3). It is one `Node` with `process_mode = PROCESS_MODE_ALWAYS` and `process_priority = ProcessPriority.PRESENTATION`, set from code, and it holds the `PresentationDriver` (`RefCounted`, no scene tree) that the composition root constructs and injects (ADR-0008 § 6.2). Its single `_process(delta)` does, in this order: (1) advance `present_time` (frozen while the kernel is `PAUSED`), (2) the zoom cooldown, (3) the `RESCALING` re-derive if dirty, (4) `driver.frame(delta, present_time)`. **No second node runs at `PRESENTATION` for presentation work**, so the priority-0 tie is removed by construction rather than by tree order, and `present_time` is current when the driver runs (this closes the host and ordering questions that earlier drafts left to ADR-0008). **Presenters define no `_process`.** They register a `PresenterDescriptor` with the driver in `BOOTING`; the driver freezes the registry with the kernel and sorts it once by stage.
191	
192	This is the "explicit driver" the HUD GDD asks for (OQ-HS-44, OQ-HS-51, ADR candidate F). It replaces N nodes whose relative order would depend on priority sub-constants and tree order with one loop over a fixed-size array, which is testable headless with stub presenters (AC-HS-89) and does not depend on the cross-node `process_priority` result for any presenter. Only the order **host after TickDriver** depends on ADR-0001's verified order, which the windowed 4.7.2 editor run confirmed and KRN-LAT-02 confirms on a desktop release export.
193	
194	**Why the solve is in the driver and not in `frame_pre_draw`.** The windowed probe shows `frame_pre_draw` firing after every node `_process`, so a camera solve placed inside it is invisible to the HUD stage and gives the HUD a one-frame lag on `world_to_hud`. The solve therefore runs in stage `CAMERA_SOLVE`, and the `frame_pre_draw` handler only writes `canvas_transform` and the parallax offsets from the solved pose. **Fallback**, used only if `frame_pre_draw` fails the release-export spike (ADR-0008 pipeline spike step 12): that write moves to the end of `PipelineRoot._process`, after `driver.frame`; no new priority constant is needed.
195	
196	```gdscript
197	# src/presentation/pipeline/presentation_stage.gd (no new directory: the shared files live in the existing Pipeline module, ADR-0010)
198	# Named constants only; nobody writes a literal stage number.
199	class_name PresentationStage extends RefCounted
200	const PROJECT: int = 0         # PROJECTOR builds and rebuilds, chunked: layout projector, body.projector, then the occluder builder
201	const CAMERA_SOLVE: int = 1    # CameraSolver computes pose_q and world_to_hud; the canvas write is in frame_pre_draw
202	const AVATAR: int = 2          # Avatar Presenter: position, frame, flip, beam pose
203	const FILTER: int = 3          # Perception Filter step, decoy list, perceived() memo
204	const INSTRUMENTS: int = 4
205	const HUD: int = 5
206	const LIGHTING: int = 6        # reads the beam pose (AVATAR) and the decoy list (FILTER)
207	const TRAIL: int = 7           # Failure & Trail (truth channel, reads no Filter product)
208	const AUDIO: int = 8
209	const DEBUG: int = 9
210	
211	# src/presentation/pipeline/presentation_discontinuity.gd
212	class_name PresentationDiscontinuity extends RefCounted
213	const RESTORE: int = 0         # restore, cold load or new game: PresentationClock.load_seq changed
214	const CAMERA_CUT: int = 1      # the camera stage called driver.notify_camera_cut()
215	```
216	
217	**Stage 0 holds three registrants, and their order is declared, not incidental.** The layout projector, `body.projector` and Lighting's occluder builder all register at `PROJECT`. The occluder builder depends on the tiles the layout projector builds, so a tie would otherwise be an order that varies. `Array.sort_custom` is not stable in Godot (probed, § Engine Compatibility), so the driver does **not** sort descriptors with a comparator: `freeze()` builds one packed integer key per descriptor, `stage * 1024 + registration_index`, sorts the `Array[int]` with plain `Array.sort()` (ADR-0005 § 1.7's recommendation) and runs the descriptors in key order. Within a stage the order is therefore **registration order, fixed by the composition root**, and a descriptor that needs a same-stage predecessor names it in `after`; `freeze()` fails boot if a named predecessor is not registered earlier in the same stage. The composition root registers the layout projector, then `body.projector`, then the occluder builder.
218	
219	**The pinned partial order and why this total order satisfies it.** Every source that states an edge is satisfied:
220	- HUD AC-HS-89 and TR-hud-022: camera solver, Avatar Presenter, Filter, HUD, Lighting. Stages 1, 2, 3, 5, 6.
221	- PF-35 and TR-percfilter-025: Avatar, then Filter, then Lighting reads the decoy list. Stages 2, 3, 6.
222	- TR-pc-040: the Presenter's beam pose is written before Lighting applies. Stages 2, 6.
223	- Instruments call `perceived()`, so they follow the Filter. Stages 3, 4.
224	- The rest (Trail, Audio, Debug after Lighting) is a convention. It differs from the order in `architecture.md` § Data Flow (Avatar, Lighting, Trail, Instruments, HUD, Audio), which the three GDD-stated edges override; § GDD sync lists the rewrite. The technical-director ruled (TD-22) that this stage order stands because it satisfies AC-HS-89 and PF-35.
225	- **Camera versus Avatar.** Pipeline C2 asks for the camera "ordered after the actor" so that both compose the same interpolated position. This ADR gets the same guarantee by construction, not by order: the solver and the Avatar Presenter both call `Placement.at` with the same `PresentFrame` values, so they cannot disagree. The solver runs first because the HUD needs `world_to_hud` before it draws (TR-hud-022). Step 12 of the pipeline spike (zero render-px disagreement) tests the claim.
226	
227	```gdscript
228	# src/presentation/pipeline/presenter_descriptor.gd
229	# RefCounted by rule: a descriptor that became a Node or Resource would collide `name` with Node.name / Resource.resource_name.
230	class_name PresenterDescriptor extends RefCounted
231	var name: StringName
232	var stage: int                        # a PresentationStage constant
233	var reads: Array[int]                 # stages whose products this presenter calls; each must be < stage
234	var after: Array[StringName]          # same-stage presenters that must be registered earlier (intra-stage order); usually empty
235	var present: Callable                 # (frame: PresentFrame) -> void; standard method Callable, exactly one argument
236	var on_discontinuity: Callable        # (kind: int) -> void; kind is a PresentationDiscontinuity constant; standard method Callable, exactly one argument
237	
238	# src/presentation/pipeline/present_frame.gd
239	class_name PresentFrame extends RefCounted     # one object, reused every frame; fields overwritten, never reallocated
240	var alpha: float            # clock.tick_alpha read ONCE per frame; in [0, 1]; 1.0 while not RUNNING
241	var T: int                  # last committed tick; may feed values the simulation also computes, never cosmetic phase
242	var running: bool
243	var present_time: float     # supplied by PipelineRoot (ADR-0008); frozen while PAUSED; the only cosmetic clock
244	var present_delta: float    # present_time minus the previous frame's present_time; 0.0 while PAUSED; drives manual animation advance (§ 5)
245	var render_delta: float     # engine _process delta, scaled by Engine.time_scale, CLAMPED by the driver to ADR-0008's DT_MAX; smoothing filters only, never a phase
246	
247	# src/presentation/pipeline/presentation_driver.gd
248	class_name PresentationDriver extends RefCounted
249	func register(desc: PresenterDescriptor) -> void          # BOOTING only
250	func freeze() -> void                                      # builds packed stage*1024+index keys, Array.sort(); fails boot on any check below
251	func frame(host_delta: float, present_time: float) -> void # fills PresentFrame, handles load_seq, runs the stages
252	func notify_camera_cut() -> void                           # called by the camera stage; next frame every presenter gets CAMERA_CUT
253	```
254	
255	**`freeze()` checks, all boot failures:** names are unique; every `reads` entry is strictly less than the descriptor's `stage`; every `after` name is a presenter of the same stage registered earlier; `present.is_valid()`, `present.is_standard()` and `present.get_argument_count() == 1`; and the same three for `on_discontinuity`. `present` and `on_discontinuity` are untyped `Callable`s, so without the arity check a wrong signature would fail only at call time on the first frame the presenter runs (`Callable.get_argument_count` exists in 4.7.2, probed).
256	
257	`present` and `on_discontinuity` are registered `Callable`s returning `void`. They are **not** kernel-invoked owner callables, so ADR-0003's `CompletionToken` rule does not apply to them, and registering `Callable`s rather than overriding a base class avoids the 4.7 typed-return override rule altogether (ADR-0003 § 1 makes the same choice for owners). That rule would bite only if a base presenter class declared a typed non-void virtual for handlers, which this ADR forbids unless ADR-0010 introduces one with the conditions in Implementation Guidelines. A `-> void` override under an `@abstract` base needs no `return`.
258	
259	**`render_delta` and `present_time`.** Both derive from the engine's `_process` delta, which is scaled by `Engine.time_scale` and arrives as one huge value after a main-loop stall (a Windows window drag or resize, focus loss, a shader-compile hitch). The driver therefore clamps `render_delta` to the same `DT_MAX` as ADR-0008's camera solver, so a smoothing filter fed it does not jump. `present_time` itself advances by whatever ADR-0008 says (this ADR does not decide whether a stall advances it); `present_delta` is whatever `present_time` advanced.
260	
261	**Driver rules.** The driver iterates a fixed-size array, allocates nothing, checks `present.is_valid()` before each call and skips and counts a freed presenter (`PRESENTER_DEAD`, as ADR-0002 does for result handlers), and **never runs a presenter inside a tick**. Presenter faults cannot fault the kernel: nothing here runs in a tick phase. Stage timing exists in dev and playtest builds through ADR-0001's diagnostics timer and is compiled out of release.
262	
263	**The frame object is the clock.** `PresentFrame.alpha` is read once; no presenter reads `PresentationClock.tick_alpha` directly (a lint allows the `tick_alpha` read only in `presentation_driver.gd`, ADR-0010 TD-17; tests inject a `PresentFrame`, and the camera solver's pure-function twin takes alpha as an argument). This guarantees one alpha per frame. A presenter may read `frame.T` for values the simulation also computes (the beacon aim at `T`, a Graph step index); it **must never** use `T` or any tick counter as cosmetic phase (registry `cosmetic_phase_from_tick_counter`), and uses `frame.present_time` for cosmetic phase.
264	
265	**Pause.** `PresentFrame.present_time` is frozen while the kernel is `PAUSED` and `alpha` is 1.0, so a presenter that computes from `present_time` and `alpha` is frozen without being told. Layers 3 and 4 (Chart Table) keep running on engine time because they must respond while paused (PR-9); they are INPUT_SURFACE objects and UI Controls, not world presenters.
266	
267	**The `_process` rule and its exemption set (this ADR owns the set; ADR-0010 PRES-01 is reworded to match, TD-02).** `_process` and `_physics_process` are forbidden in any object registered through `PresenterDescriptor`. They are allowed only in `PipelineRoot` (the `PresentationHost`), `INPUT_SURFACE` objects at `ProcessPriority.INPUT_ADAPTER`, and layer 3 and 4 UI Controls. The shared files in this section (`presentation_stage.gd`, `presentation_discontinuity.gd`, `presenter_descriptor.gd`, `present_frame.gd`, `presentation_driver.gd`, `placement.gd`) live in `src/presentation/pipeline/`, an existing module directory, so ARCH-01 and `modules.json` need no change and presentation-to-presentation imports are already allowed (ruling TD-02). There is no separate `PresentationHost` file.
268	
269	### 4. Integer placement at `tick_alpha`
270	
271	One function, one owner, no other rounding anywhere in presentation.
272	
273	```gdscript
274	# src/presentation/pipeline/placement.gd
275	class_name Placement extends RefCounted
276	## Interpolate previous to current at alpha, then floor, per axis. alpha is clamped by the caller's PresentFrame.
277	static func at(prev: Vector2i, curr: Vector2i, alpha: float) -> Vector2i:
278		return Vector2i(floori(prev.x + (curr.x - prev.x) * alpha), floori(prev.y + (curr.y - prev.y) * alpha))
279	
280	## Alpha for a block whose owner runs every n ticks and publishes the tick it last ran (Horror alpha_5, PR-9).
281	static func alpha_n(run_tick: int, T: int, alpha: float, n: int) -> float:
282		return clampf((float(T - run_tick) + alpha) / float(n), 0.0, 1.0)
283	
284	## Floor a float vector to whole pixels, per axis. The integer helper for derived offsets that are not a prev/curr pair
285	## (the camera host's parallax layer offsets are built from this, never from a bare floor(); ADR-0008 § 6.2).
286	static func floor_v(v: Vector2) -> Vector2i:
287		return Vector2i(floori(v.x), floori(v.y))
288	
289	## The only assignment point for a Node2D position in presentation. Skips an unchanged write.
290	static func put(node: Node2D, p: Vector2i) -> void:
291		var v: Vector2 = Vector2(p)
292		if node.position != v:
293			node.position = v
294	
295	## The same for a Control: HUD plates that follow world things (layer 2) are Controls (ADR-0008 § 5.5), and Control has no Node2D.position.
296	static func put_control(c: Control, p: Vector2i) -> void:
297		var v: Vector2 = Vector2(p)
298		if c.position != v:
299			c.position = v
300	```
301	
302	**Rules:**
303	- Every moving thing in the current body frame is placed with `Placement.at` and written with `Placement.put` (a `Node2D`) or `Placement.put_control` (a `Control`): sprites, the avatar, hand tools, the beam chest point, light origins, **HUD world-anchored plates (layer 2, written with `put_control`)**, the single floored canvas offset of a non-avatar body (`Placement.at(off_prev, off_curr, alpha)` with both offsets taken relative to the avatar's body, TR-shipbody-033), and the camera pose. The beam's chest point and the Avatar sprite use the same rounded position, so light origin and sprite never disagree (PR-4 rule 2, TR-pc-026).
304	- **`floori`, never `int()`, `round`, `roundi` or truncation.** Probed 2026-10-28: `floori(-3 + 1 * 0.5)` is -3. Truncation and rounding both move negative-coordinate bodies by a pixel relative to positive ones.
305	- **Interpolate, then quantise (PR-4 rule 3).** Snap is a floor, not a filter: a body moving one base pixel per tick shows a k by k block step at interpolated timing, never twice in a frame at 60 fps and above, never backward. Nothing is rounded before the lerp.
306	- `alpha` is `frame.alpha`, in [0, 1], never extrapolated. `alpha_n` is legal only for a block whose owner publishes its run tick, is clamped at 1, and is floored by `at`. The sprite pose of a stepped rig (Horror) is not tweened; only the record's position is placed with `alpha_n` (PR-9).
307	- **Placement lint, scoped to what the decision covers.** The lint applies to `Node2D` and `Control` nodes under the world viewport's layer 0 and to the HUD's world-anchored plates (layer 2). Writes to a node's position, global position, offset or transform appear only in `placement.gd` and in the **named allow-list** below. The lint must cover the whole engine API surface, not a naive `position =` regex: besides assignment, the position is also written through `set_position()`, `set_global_position()`, `set_transform()`, `set_global_transform()`, `translate()`, `global_translate()`, `move_local_x()`, `move_local_y()`, `set_offset()`, `set("position")`, `Sprite2D.offset`, and through `AnimationPlayer` or `Tween` property tracks on those names. ADR-0010 owns the mechanics (TD-17): a token ban on those calls and on `global_position =` and `offset =` outside the allow-list; a resource scan rejecting `Animation` tracks on `:position`, `:global_position`, `:offset` or `:transform`, and `tween_property` calls on those names, for presentation nodes; the `sort_custom` ban extended to `src/presentation/pipeline/`; and the `tick_alpha` read confined to `presentation_driver.gd`.
308	- **Allow-list (TD-18).** Outside `placement.gd` the following legitimately write geometry: `src/presentation/pipeline/viewport_wiring.gd` (`WorldContainer.position`, `HudRoot.size`, layer geometry) and the camera host's `frame_pre_draw` handler (the world viewport `canvas_transform` and the parallax layer offsets). **Parallax offsets keep Placement's integer math**: the handler builds them from `Placement.floor_v` (a `Vector2i` from `floori`), not from a bare `-floor(...)`; ADR-0008 § 6.2 adopts that form. Layer 3 and 4 UI Controls (Chart Table, menus) keep their own layout idioms and are outside the lint (PR-9, ADR-0030), because they are laid out by the Control system, not placed from sim state.
309	- **The post-frame sweep reads `global_position`, not `position`.** A debug-build and integration-test sweep reads every `Node2D` and world-anchored `Control` under the world root once per frame in the scripted walk and asserts that `global_position` is integral within an epsilon of 0 (`PLACEMENT_FRACTIONAL` counts, test fails on non-zero). Local `position` is not enough: a parent at an odd offset, or a centred `Sprite2D` with an odd-sized texture (a 0.5 px offset), makes the drawn origin fractional even when local `position` is integral, so the sweep also checks the centred-plus-offset case. `Node2D.position` is a 32-bit `Vector2`, so integer exactness holds only up to 2^24 px, which is ample for this map.
310	- No per-node scale animation; horizontal flip is `flip_h` or a scale of -1 on x only; `Camera2D.zoom` stays (1, 1); rotation of human-built geometry is 0 (PR-4 rules 4 and 5). Cosmetic offsets (tremor of plus or minus 1 art px) are integers added after placement.
311	- `snap_2d_transforms_to_pixel` and `snap_2d_vertices_to_pixel` are on as a safety net, set to their required values in `project.godot` by the Pipeline's guard rails (PR-15; probed: both default `false`). **Nothing in this ADR relies on them**; they snap in base-pixel space under pass B and `canvas_transform` is in base-pixel units (ADR-0008 § 2.2 and § 4).
312	- An asset or one-off sprite uses even cell dimensions or `centered = false` with an integer `offset` (PR-4 rule 6); the asset lint is ADR-0010's, and it also carries the animation-resource scan above.
313	
314	### 5. One interpolator: physics interpolation off, and no engine clock on sim-visible content
315	
316	**The pins.** `physics/common/physics_interpolation` is **absent or `false` in `project.godot`**; the effective value is checked through `ProjectSettings.get_setting` in the post-first-frame boot check and in a gdUnit4 test (ADR-0008 § 5.5(a), effective-value tier), because a value equal to the default is not serialised and a `ConfigFile` read cannot confirm an absent key's effective value (TD-21; ADR-0010 PRJ-02 moves this key from presence checks to the effective-value tier). The presentation root nodes set `physics_interpolation_mode = Node.PHYSICS_INTERPOLATION_MODE_OFF` (value 2; the bare word `OFF` is not valid GDScript) and children inherit. `Camera2D.position_smoothing_enabled = false` and `limit_smoothed = false` where a `Camera2D` exists at all (the primary camera variant has none in the world tree, PR-6 C2).
317	
318	**The boot check, after the first `SceneTree.process_frame`** (probed: inheritance propagates lazily, so a read before the first frame can disagree with a read after it, and a node added later reads correctly immediately): `ProjectSettings.get_setting("physics/common/physics_interpolation") == false`, `get_tree().physics_interpolation == false`, and a walk over every node under the presentation roots asserts `not node.is_physics_interpolated()`. Because `is_physics_interpolated()` **ignores the global enable flag** (probed), the walk asserts explicit `OFF` inheritance from an `OFF` root, not effective interpolation, and that is why the roots must be explicit `OFF`. A violation fails boot in dev and playtest builds and counts `PHYSICS_INTERPOLATION_ON` plus logs in release. A gdUnit4 test additionally turns `SceneTree.physics_interpolation` on, builds the presentation tree, and asserts `is_physics_interpolated_and_enabled()` is false for every node, which proves the `OFF` roots rather than only the project setting.
319	
320	**Why not use the engine's 2D interpolation.** (a) It would be a second interpolator on a second clock (PR-4 rule 8). (b) Probed: `get_global_transform_interpolated` does not exist on `Node2D`, so no script could read where an engine-interpolated body is actually drawn, and the camera, which follows the un-interpolated pose, would swim against the sprite by 1 to 3 render pixels at 144 fps while looking fine at 60. (c) The kernel's previous and current pair is the only definition of the previous pose that survives a restore, a body transfer and a snap (`snap_baseline`, ADR-0003).
321	
322	**Engine clocks on sim-visible content.** `Tween`, `AnimationPlayer`, `AnimatedSprite2D.play()` and `GPUParticles2D` at a non-zero `speed_scale` run on the engine's process time, which does not stop under kernel `PAUSED` (the tree is not paused, ADR-0001 § 6) and does not follow reduced motion. For world content (layer 0) and the HUD (layer 2) a presenter therefore drives animation from `frame.present_time`:
323	- **Primary pattern, `AnimationPlayer`:** set `callback_mode_process = AnimationMixer.ANIMATION_CALLBACK_MODE_PROCESS_MANUAL` and call `advance(frame.present_delta)` from `present`. Probed on 4.7.2: this works exactly, and it is frozen under `PAUSED` (`present_delta` is 0) by construction, and a reduced-motion rule applied to `present_delta` or the played animation reaches it like any other `present_time`-driven content, with no engine clock involved.
324	- **`AnimatedSprite2D`:** set `frame` and `frame_progress` from `frame.present_time` (a frame index computed from it); do not rely on `speed_scale`.
325	- **Shader time:** a shader parameter set from `frame.present_time`.
326	- **Particles:** call `restart()` in `on_discontinuity(RESTORE)` so no stale emission survives a restore, new game or camera cut; freeze under `PAUSED` with `speed_scale = 0` as a fallback only. The class docs say 0 pauses a `GPUParticles2D`, but the dummy renderer cannot simulate particles, so this is UNVERIFIED and is a story-level check on the first story that freezes particles (§ Validation); the stronger alternative is to avoid sim-visible particles on layer 0 and layer 2.
327	- **`speed_scale = 0` as a fallback** for `AnimationPlayer` and `Tween` is probed (neither advances), but it is not the primary pattern, because `PROCESS_MANUAL` plus `advance` is exact and needs no clock reasoning.
328	Engine-clocked animation is permitted only on layers 3 and 4 (Chart Table and menus), which must respond under pause, and on content that has no sim-visible meaning and is allowed to continue.
329	
330	The bounded presentation-owned animation states are those PR-8 admits (camera state, and the instruments' `settle_response`), plus the cosmetic scalars of § 6.
331	
332	### 6. Presentation-local state, the restore edge, and pure-function presenters
333	
334	**What presentation may keep.** A presenter may hold a scalar or small structure (a needle's settle triple, a dwell counter, a tremor envelope, a fade, a cull history, the camera's smoothing state, a numeral throttle) **if and only if**:
335	1. it is never persisted, hashed, replicated or read by the simulation (`src/kernel/` and `src/sim/` import nothing from `src/presentation/`);
336	2. it changes how a value *arrives* and never what it *settles to*, and never decides visibility of a truth-channel element (a trail's visibility depends only on the sim, which is why the Failure & Trail GDD calls it a pure reader);
337	3. it is reset by `on_discontinuity` on a restore, a new game, a camera cut and `hard_start` (TR-instr-002, TR-attention-047);
338	4. the presenter's registration lists it in a short doc comment so a reviewer can see the scalars (the lint cannot).
339	
340	**A presenter's drawn output is a pure function** of `(PresentationViews at this frame, PresentFrame, its resettable scalars)`. The first frame after a restore needs no special path: `ALL` rebuilds from views, `on_discontinuity(RESTORE)` clears the scalars, and the kernel's `snap_baseline` has made previous equal current, so there is no interpolation across the break (TR-cmd-046, TR-horror-041, TR-attention-047, TR-webmap-039 restore half). A multi-beat stall plays at most one beat and never replays (TR-attention-047): a presenter keeps the last-seen sequence value it was shown, compares it with the view's, and on a jump of more than one shows the end state.
341	
342	**Edge detection by sequence counters.** A presenter detects a discrete source change by comparing a view's sequence counter to the value it last saw (`breath_src_change_seq`, TR-suit-041), not by counting notifications, because merged delivery turns N ticks into one batch. Because the notification, the dirty mark and the draw happen in one rendered frame, a click can start in the Audio stage and the dial swap land in the Instruments stage of the same frame.
343	
344	**The restore edge is not `ALL`.** `ALL` also means "more than 256 keys changed this frame" (a weld can do it), and resetting an instrument's tremor on a weld is wrong. The driver therefore watches a dedicated counter, part of one combined amendment this ADR requests of ADR-0001 (TD-04), which also covers the Pipeline's kernel-state need:
345	
346	```gdscript
347	# Requested of ADR-0001's PresentationClock (read-only, not a state block, never hashed or saved; backed by the TickDriver):
348	var state: int       # the KernelState enum, read-only (the Pipeline's RUNNING / PAUSED / SAVING / LOADING / FAULTED need; no KernelStateView type)
349	var load_seq: int    # +1 on every LOADING -> RUNNING transition, restore and new game and cold load alike, immediately before
350	                     # deliver_all; never on PAUSED -> RUNNING or SAVING -> RUNNING; never hashed or saved
351	```
352	
353	`load_seq` is backed by the kernel or TickDriver, not by the presentation driver, and ADR-0004 shows a new game also going `LOADING` to `RUNNING`, so no separate "and on every new game" rule exists. A cold Continue at boot is a `LOADING` to `RUNNING` transition and bumps it. ADR-0006's `restore_epoch` cannot substitute: it does not advance on Save & Quit then Continue (ADR-0006 § 3.2), and it is read only inside `RngFacet.draw_epoch`. ADR-0008 reads `PresentationClock.state` instead of a `KernelStateView` and takes its camera `CUT` trigger from the same `load_seq` change; **ADR-0001 is the owner of the edit and Acceptance of this ADR is gated on it being applied.**
354	
355	At the top of `frame(...)` the driver compares `clock.load_seq` with the last seen value and, on a change, calls every presenter's `on_discontinuity(PresentationDiscontinuity.RESTORE)` **before** any `present`. Camera cuts arrive the other way: the camera stage calls `driver.notify_camera_cut()` and the next frame delivers `PresentationDiscontinuity.CAMERA_CUT` (reset of instrument scalars and cull history; Instruments IW-33). `BODY_TRANSFER` is a rebase, not a cut, unless the new body's limits clamp (TR-shipbody-049, ADR-0008). The kernel's `snap_baseline` on entry to `RUNNING` (ADR-0001 § 4, ADR-0003) is the only restore-continuity mechanism for the previous/current pair; the `RESTORE` discontinuity resets presentation scalars and, for particles, restarts emission (§ 5).
356	
357	### 7. `INPUT_SURFACE` is the only submitting class, and a class is not a right
358	
359	- A command can be submitted only by an object that holds a `SurfaceHandle` (ADR-0002) **and** was registered as `INPUT_SURFACE`. Subscribing as `INPUT_SURFACE` confers no submit right (registry `presentation_submit_without_handle`): the Interaction prompt object subscribes without a handle. A `PRESENTATION` facet has no submit method and no way to obtain a handle.
360	- **Boot check at the freeze, limited to `SurfaceHandle`s:** every name passed to `issue_surface_handle` has an `INPUT_SURFACE` registration with the same name, and no `SurfaceHandle` name matches a `PRESENTATION`, `PROJECTOR` or `DIAGNOSTIC` registration. A handle issued to a name with no `INPUT_SURFACE` registration, or to a `PRESENTATION` subscriber, fails boot. **`ControlHandle`s are outside this check:** ADR-0002 uses one issued-handle table for both kinds, and `save_load` and `pause_gate` hold `ControlHandle`s without any subscription (ADR-0006 § 1.12 makes Save/Load a control-plane caller, not a subscriber). **A "registration" is the composition root's facet issue**, not a subscription: a facet issued as `INPUT_SURFACE` under a name is a registration whether or not it ever subscribes to a block, so the Input Adapter is not forced to subscribe to anything just to pass the check. ADR-0004's `subscribe` carries the diagnostic name as its `name` argument for the subscribing case.
361	- **Where a submit call may occur: the list is ADR-0002's, not restated here.** The submit sites are exactly the objects named at `issue_surface_handle` (ADR-0002; ADR-0010 KRN-04 implements the grep keyed to those names, not to a fixed file, per TD-06). **At MVP that is the Input Adapter only**, which submits from its own `_process` at `ProcessPriority.INPUT_ADAPTER`. The general `INPUT_SURFACE` rule below applies once a second `SurfaceHandle` is issued, and it is a condition attached to issuing that handle (ADR-0002): the holder **latches an intent in a plain field in its UI callback** and submits it from its own `_process` at `INPUT_ADAPTER`, so its commands are queued before the driver's tick loop and reach the same tick as the Adapter's. It **never** calls `submit` from an engine signal handler, `_gui_input`, `_input`, `_physics_process`, a notification handler or a `PRESENTATION` object. This is a wider rule than ADR-0001's "submit input only from the Input Adapter's `_process`", which is correct at MVP; the widening is a post-MVP condition, not a statement of current fact. The control plane is different: `ControlHandle` calls are recorded when made, from any phase (CR-15), so a UI button calling `PauseGate` from its signal handler is legal. This ADR therefore adds no second submit location and no driver stage for submission.
362	- **Result handlers.** The kernel flushes the result buffer in the driver, before presentation; an `INPUT_SURFACE` result handler is a kernel-invoked callable and obeys the same contract as a subscriber handler: it records the result into a fixed ring and returns `ctx.complete()`. Display of a rejection happens in the object's own presenter step (the stage it is registered for), never in the handler.
363	- **The rule is per object, not per system** (CR-10): a HUD that grows a button splits into the HUD presenter (`PRESENTATION`) and a small `INPUT_SURFACE` intent object.
364	- Presentation predicts no outcome; the Adapter's pre-play of body motion and sound keyed by `correlation` is ADR-0019's, and light and effects change only on committed state (kernel anti-target: no client-side prediction at MVP).
365	
366	### 8. Engine signals stay inside presentation
367	
368	Engine signals (`signal`, `.connect(...)`) are used **between presentation objects for user-initiated events only** (a card opens, a setting changes, a button is pressed). They are never the kernel's notification transport (ADR-0004 § 1 decides a kernel-owned observer registry of Callables and no engine signals; this ADR agrees), never carry simulation values into a simulation module, and are never declared or connected in `src/kernel/` or `src/sim/` (a lint; the simulation is scene-tree free). A signal is not a way around the stage-read rule: a presenter that needs another presenter's per-frame product reads it through a declared `reads` edge, not through a connection.
369

110	### 1. Subscriber classes and what each may read and write
111	
112	The class is chosen by the composition root at facet-issue time, not by the presenter. A presenter cannot subscribe as a class its facet was not issued for.
113	
114	```gdscript
115	# src/kernel/facets/presentation_facet.gd (placement requested of ADR-0010, see "Facet-side types" in Key Interfaces).
116	# Issued by the composition root in BOOTING, one per presentation object, never the whole Kernel (ADR-0001 § 5).

157	### 2. Dirty-mark-then-draw
158	
159	**The handler contract.** The kernel invokes each subscriber handler through a registered `Callable` with a reused `NotifyContext` (ADR-0003 § 3), exactly like every other kernel-invoked callable. The shape is ADR-0003's, as fixed by ADR-0004 § 2 (re-read 2026-10-28; it matches):
160	
161	```gdscript
162	func _on_changes(batch: ChangeBatch, ctx: NotifyContext) -> CompletionToken:
163		_dirty.absorb(batch)        # ADR-0004 DirtyAccumulator (capacity facet.key_capacity); allocates nothing; is_all on overflow
164		return ctx.complete()       # last statement; nothing follows it
165	```
166	
167	This replaces the architecture document's `-> void` example (§ GDD sync). A handler **must** do only this: copy the batch's keys into the presenter's pre-sized dirty structure, copy the scalar fields it needs from an event record into a fixed-size ring, and return. A handler **must never**: read a view, touch a node, create a `Callable` or a container, emit an engine signal, `await`, call `submit`, or write any property. A handler returns its `CompletionToken` synchronously, so `await` is banned **lexically** in any script registered through a `PresenterDescriptor` or that calls `.subscribe(` (ADR-0010 PRES rule, TD-16, with a bad fixture); the kernel's token-identity check is the runtime backstop and records anything other than the armed token, including a suspended coroutine state, as `INCOMPLETE` (ADR-0004 § 2), which counts against the handler. A handler fault is counted and never fatal (ADR-0003).
168	
169	**Why the handler does not draw.** It runs inside P5 with writes disabled and its cost is added to every other subscriber's; a catch-up frame already runs the tick loop up to four times (`MAX_TICKS_PER_FRAME`) and `INPUT_SURFACE` handlers run once per tick. Reading views there would also read a state that a later tick in the same frame is about to replace.
170	
171	**Delivery recap (properties this ADR relies on; ADR-0004 owns the mechanism):**
172	- PRESENTATION, PROJECTOR and DIAGNOSTIC batches arrive **once per rendered frame**, after the frame's last tick, one `ChangeBatch` per dirty block per subscription, with the union of the frame's keys (`is_all` true past `MAX_DIRTY_KEYS` 256; this text's "`ALL`" means `batch.is_all`). INPUT_SURFACE and REPLICATION get every tick's batch. A 0-tick frame delivers nothing.
173	- A restore delivers one `is_all` batch per block to every class when `LOADING` becomes `RUNNING`, with `batch.tick` set to the restored `T` (ADR-0004 P5/load delivery). **`ChangeBatch` carries no load marker, by design** (ADR-0004 § 6 states it; see `PresentationClock.load_seq`), so `is_all` is indistinguishable from a mass change; the restore edge is `load_seq` (§ 6).
174	- Notifications carry no state; event records (`BODY_TRANSFER`, `POD_ARRIVED`, `DERELICT_LOADED`) carry identifiers only.
175	
176	**The draw side.** Each presenter keeps two things, and its `present(frame)` early-outs only when both are empty:
177	- `dirty`: which blocks or keys changed since its last draw. Dirty drives **bulk and structural reads** (lists, queries, rebuilds, layout of plates): a presenter performs a bulk read of a block only when that block, or `ALL`, is dirty (TR-instr-005: derived inputs refresh once per Graph step because the Graph dirties its keys once per step, never per frame).
178	- `animating`: whether anything still moves on `tick_alpha` or `present_time` (an interpolated position, a needle ramp, a fade, flow scroll). **Interpolation needs a draw on frames with no notification**, because a 144 fps frame between two ticks has a new `tick_alpha` and no new state; the example in `architecture.md` that returns when `_dirty.is_empty()` would freeze motion on those frames and is corrected. Cheap scalar getters on the `interpolated` pair (previous and current position) may be read every frame while `animating`.
179	- `ALL` means "rebuild everything from the views, and draw the end state with no transition": the correct and sufficient response both to a restore and to a mass change. A presenter bounds a rebuild by its own budget (PROJECTOR: `BUILD_TILES_PER_FRAME`, chunked across frames, continuing to draw the last complete state until the chunks finish). One exception, stated in § 1 (amended 2026-10-29, sync knock-on fix, round 3): Lighting's occluder builder rebuilds a section intersecting an active shadow light's reach disc as one chunk outside the `BUILD_TILES_PER_FRAME` slice and applies its polygons to the pooled `LightOccluder2D` nodes in a single apply at the end of its last chunk, so stage 0 finishes before `LIGHTING` (stage 6) in the same frame; every other occluder rebuild keeps the old complete set drawing until the final apply, and the frames in between are counted event frames.
180	- Event records are copied into a fixed ring; ring overflow degrades to a full rebuild and counts `PRESENTER_EVENT_OVERFLOW`. Events are never dropped silently, and a `BODY_TRANSFER` is delivered to the camera as a rebase, not a cut (TR-shipbody-049; the rebase math is ADR-0008's).
181	
182	**Coherence by construction.** The driver runs inside `PipelineRoot._process` at `PRESENTATION` (0), after the TickDriver (-50) in the same `_process` pass, and the kernel cannot tick while presentation runs, so every presenter in a frame reads the same committed tick `T`. No presenter copies state to be consistent.
183	
184	**Latency, stated honestly.** Discrete committed state (a bead appears, a light toggles) is drawn in the same rendered frame as the P5 that announced it, with zero frames of delay (TR-assembly-045). Continuously interpolated motion lags the commit by up to one tick by construction, because `tick_alpha` is clamped at 1 and never extrapolates (PR-4 rule 3, PR-9 rate table).
185	
186	**A debug-build safety net, in addition to ADR-0004's check that every changed block marked a dirty key.** A presenter that applies **key-level incremental updates** (the PROJECTOR chunks, the Trail, Lighting's occluder builder) exposes `rebuild_signature() -> int` in debug and test builds only (a hash of its derived draw model). The dirty-correctness test (Validation) runs a scripted command stream through that incrementally updated presenter and a fresh presenter fed `ALL`, and requires equal signatures. A presenter that forgot to react to a key is caught by that test, not in play. A presenter that rebuilds a whole block whenever any of its keys is dirty is **exempt**, because the equivalence proves nothing for it. This is a story-level definition-of-done item for the presenter's story that references this ADR, not a blanket ADR requirement.

188	### 3. One driver, one frame object, fixed named stages
189	
190	**`PipelineRoot` is the `PresentationHost`** (ruling TD-03; ADR-0008 owns the edit to its § 6.1, § 6.2 and § 7.3). It is one `Node` with `process_mode = PROCESS_MODE_ALWAYS` and `process_priority = ProcessPriority.PRESENTATION`, set from code, and it holds the `PresentationDriver` (`RefCounted`, no scene tree) that the composition root constructs and injects (ADR-0008 § 6.2). Its single `_process(delta)` does, in this order: (1) advance `present_time` (frozen while the kernel is `PAUSED`), (2) the zoom cooldown, (3) the `RESCALING` re-derive if dirty, (4) `driver.frame(delta, present_time)`. **No second node runs at `PRESENTATION` for presentation work**, so the priority-0 tie is removed by construction rather than by tree order, and `present_time` is current when the driver runs (this closes the host and ordering questions that earlier drafts left to ADR-0008). **Presenters define no `_process`.** They register a `PresenterDescriptor` with the driver in `BOOTING`; the driver freezes the registry with the kernel and sorts it once by stage.

192	This is the "explicit driver" the HUD GDD asks for (OQ-HS-44, OQ-HS-51, ADR candidate F). 279	
280	## Alpha for a block whose owner runs every n ticks and publishes the tick it last ran (Horror alpha_5, PR-9).
281	static func alpha_n(run_tick: int, T: int, alpha: float, n: int) -> float:
282		return clampf((float(T - run_tick) + alpha) / float(n), 0.0, 1.0)
283	
284	## Floor a float vector to whole pixels, per axis. The integer helper for derived offsets that are not a prev/curr pair
285	## (the camera host's parallax layer offsets are built from this, never from a bare floor(); ADR-0008 § 6.2).
286	static func floor_v(v: Vector2) -> Vector2i:
287		return Vector2i(floori(v.x), floori(v.y))
288	
289	## The only assignment point for a Node2D position in presentation. Skips an unchanged write.
290	static func put(node: Node2D, p: Vector2i) -> void:
291		var v: Vector2 = Vector2(p)
292		if node.position != v:
293			node.position = v
294	
295	## The same for a Control: HUD plates that follow world things (layer 2) are Controls (ADR-0008 § 5.5), and Control has no Node2D.position.
296	static func put_control(c: Control, p: Vector2i) -> void:
297		var v: Vector2 = Vector2(p)
298		if c.position != v:
299			c.position = v
300	```
301	
302	**Rules:**
303	- Every moving thing in the current body frame is placed with `Placement.at` and written with `Placement.put` (a `Node2D`) or `Placement.put_control` (a `Control`): sprites, the avatar, hand tools, the beam chest point, light origins, **HUD world-anchored plates (layer 2, written with `put_control`)**, the single floored canvas offset of a non-avatar body (`Placement.at(off_prev, off_curr, alpha)` with both offsets taken relative to the avatar's body, TR-shipbody-033), and the camera pose. The beam's chest point and the Avatar sprite use the same rounded position, so light origin and sprite never disagree (PR-4 rule 2, TR-pc-026).
304	- **`floori`, never `int()`, `round`, `roundi` or truncation.** Probed 2026-10-28: `floori(-3 + 1 * 0.5)` is -3. Truncation and rounding both move negative-coordinate bodies by a pixel relative to positive ones.
305	- **Interpolate, then quantise (PR-4 rule 3).** Snap is a floor, not a filter: a body moving one base pixel per tick shows a k by k block step at interpolated timing, never twice in a frame at 60 fps and above, never backward. Nothing is rounded before the lerp.
306	- `alpha` is `frame.alpha`, in [0, 1], never extrapolated. `alpha_n` is legal only for a block whose owner publishes its run tick, is clamped at 1, and is floored by `at`. The sprite pose of a stepped rig (Horror) is not tweened; only the record's position is placed with `alpha_n` (PR-9).
307	- **Placement lint, scoped to what the decision covers.** The lint applies to `Node2D` and `Control` nodes under the world viewport's layer 0 and to the HUD's world-anchored plates (layer 2). Writes to a node's position, global position, offset or transform appear only in `placement.gd` and in the **named allow-list** below. The lint must cover the whole engine API surface, not a naive `position =` regex: besides assignment, the position is also written through `set_position()`, `set_global_position()`, `set_transform()`, `set_global_transform()`, `translate()`, `global_translate()`, `move_local_x()`, `move_local_y()`, `set_offset()`, `set("position")`, `Sprite2D.offset`, and through `AnimationPlayer` or `Tween` property tracks on those names. ADR-0010 owns the mechanics (TD-17): a token ban on those calls and on `global_position =` and `offset =` outside the allow-list; a resource scan rejecting `Animation` tracks on `:position`, `:global_position`, `:offset` or `:transform`, and `tween_property` calls on those names, for presentation nodes; the `sort_custom` ban extended to `src/presentation/pipeline/`; and the `tick_alpha` read confined to `presentation_driver.gd`.
308	- **Allow-list (TD-18).** Outside `placement.gd` the following legitimately write geometry: `src/presentation/pipeline/viewport_wiring.gd` (`WorldContainer.position`, `HudRoot.size`, layer geometry) and the camera host's `frame_pre_draw` handler (the world viewport `canvas_transform` and the parallax layer offsets). **Parallax offsets keep Placement's integer math**: the handler builds them from `Placement.floor_v` (a `Vector2i` from `floori`), not from a bare `-floor(...)`; ADR-0008 § 6.2 adopts that form. Layer 3 and 4 UI Controls (Chart Table, menus) keep their own layout idioms and are outside the lint (PR-9, ADR-0030), because they are laid out by the Control system, not placed from sim state.
309	- **The post-frame sweep reads `global_position`, not `position`.** A debug-build and integration-test sweep reads every `Node2D` and world-anchored `Control` under the world root once per frame in the scripted walk and asserts that `global_position` is integral within an epsilon of 0 (`PLACEMENT_FRACTIONAL` counts, test fails on non-zero). Local `position` is not enough: a parent at an odd offset, or a centred `Sprite2D` with an odd-sized texture (a 0.5 px offset), makes the drawn origin fractional even when local `position` is integral, so the sweep also checks the centred-plus-offset case. `Node2D.position` is a 32-bit `Vector2`, so integer exactness holds only up to 2^24 px, which is ample for this map.
310	- No per-node scale animation; horizontal flip is `flip_h` or a scale of -1 on x only; `Camera2D.zoom` stays (1, 1); rotation of human-built geometry is 0 (PR-4 rules 4 and 5). Cosmetic offsets (tremor of plus or minus 1 art px) are integers added after placement.
311	- `snap_2d_transforms_to_pixel` and `snap_2d_vertices_to_pixel` are on as a safety net, set to their required values in `project.godot` by the Pipeline's guard rails (PR-15; probed: both default `false`). **Nothing in this ADR relies on them**; they snap in base-pixel space under pass B and `canvas_transform` is in base-pixel units (ADR-0008 § 2.2 and § 4).
312	- An asset or one-off sprite uses even cell dimensions or `centered = false` with an integer `offset` (PR-4 rule 6); the asset lint is ADR-0010's, and it also carries the animation-resource scan above.
313	
314	### 5. One interpolator: physics interpolation off, and no engine clock on sim-visible content
315	
316	**The pins.** `physics/common/physics_interpolation` is **absent or `false` in `project.godot`**; the effective value is checked through `ProjectSettings.get_setting` in the post-first-frame boot check and in a gdUnit4 test (ADR-0008 § 5.5(a), effective-value tier), because a value equal to the default is not serialised and a `ConfigFile` read cannot confirm an absent key's effective value (TD-21; ADR-0010 PRJ-02 moves this key from presence checks to the effective-value tier). The presentation root nodes set `physics_interpolation_mode = Node.PHYSICS_INTERPOLATION_MODE_OFF` (value 2; the bare word `OFF` is not valid GDScript) and children inherit. `Camera2D.position_smoothing_enabled = false` and `limit_smoothed = false` where a `Camera2D` exists at all (the primary camera variant has none in the world tree, PR-6 C2).
317	
318	**The boot check, after the first `SceneTree.process_frame`** (probed: inheritance propagates lazily, so a read before the first frame can disagree with a read after it, and a node added later reads correctly immediately): `ProjectSettings.get_setting("physics/common/physics_interpolation") == false`, `get_tree().physics_interpolation == false`, and a walk over every node under the presentation roots asserts `not node.is_physics_interpolated()`. Because `is_physics_interpolated()` **ignores the global enable flag** (probed), the walk asserts explicit `OFF` inheritance from an `OFF` root, not effective interpolation, and that is why the roots must be explicit `OFF`. A violation fails boot in dev and playtest builds and counts `PHYSICS_INTERPOLATION_ON` plus logs in release. A gdUnit4 test additionally turns `SceneTree.physics_interpolation` on, builds the presentation tree, and asserts `is_physics_interpolated_and_enabled()` is false for every node, which proves the `OFF` roots rather than only the project setting.
319	
320	**Why not use the engine's 2D interpolation.** (a) It would be a second interpolator on a second clock (PR-4 rule 8). (b) Probed: `get_global_transform_interpolated` does not exist on `Node2D`, so no script could read where an engine-interpolated body is actually drawn, and the camera, which follows the un-interpolated pose, would swim against the sprite by 1 to 3 render pixels at 144 fps while looking fine at 60. (c) The kernel's previous and current pair is the only definition of the previous pose that survives a restore, a body transfer and a snap (`snap_baseline`, ADR-0003).
321	
322	**Engine clocks on sim-visible content.** `Tween`, `AnimationPlayer`, `AnimatedSprite2D.play()` and `GPUParticles2D` at a non-zero `speed_scale` run on the engine's process time, which does not stop under kernel `PAUSED` (the tree is not paused, ADR-0001 § 6) and does not follow reduced motion. For world content (layer 0) and the HUD (layer 2) a presenter therefore drives animation from `frame.present_time`:
323	- **Primary pattern, `AnimationPlayer`:** set `callback_mode_process = AnimationMixer.ANIMATION_CALLBACK_MODE_PROCESS_MANUAL` and call `advance(frame.present_delta)` from `present`. Probed on 4.7.2: this works exactly, and it is frozen under `PAUSED` (`present_delta` is 0) by construction, and a reduced-motion rule applied to `present_delta` or the played animation reaches it like any other `present_time`-driven content, with no engine clock involved.
324	- **`AnimatedSprite2D`:** set `frame` and `frame_progress` from `frame.present_time` (a frame index computed from it); do not rely on `speed_scale`.
325	- **Shader time:** a shader parameter set from `frame.present_time`.
326	- **Particles:** call `restart()` in `on_discontinuity(RESTORE)` so no stale emission survives a restore, new game or camera cut; freeze under `PAUSED` with `speed_scale = 0` as a fallback only. The class docs say 0 pauses a `GPUParticles2D`, but the dummy renderer cannot simulate particles, so this is UNVERIFIED and is a story-level check on the first story that freezes particles (§ Validation); the stronger alternative is to avoid sim-visible particles on layer 0 and layer 2.
327	- **`speed_scale = 0` as a fallback** for `AnimationPlayer` and `Tween` is probed (neither advances), but it is not the primary pattern, because `PROCESS_MANUAL` plus `advance` is exact and needs no clock reasoning.
328	Engine-clocked animation is permitted only on layers 3 and 4 (Chart Table and menus), which must respond under pause, and on content that has no sim-visible meaning and is allowed to continue.
329	
330	The bounded presentation-owned animation states are those PR-8 admits (camera state, and the instruments' `settle_response`), plus the cosmetic scalars of § 6.
331	
332	### 6. Presentation-local state, the restore edge, and pure-function presenters
333	
334	**What presentation may keep.** A presenter may hold a scalar or small structure (a needle's settle triple, a dwell counter, a tremor envelope, a fade, a cull history, the camera's smoothing state, a numeral throttle) **if and only if**:
335	1. it is never persisted, hashed, replicated or read by the simulation (`src/kernel/` and `src/sim/` import nothing from `src/presentation/`);
336	2. it changes how a value *arrives* and never what it *settles to*, and never decides visibility of a truth-channel element (a trail's visibility depends only on the sim, which is why the Failure & Trail GDD calls it a pure reader);
337	3. it is reset by `on_discontinuity` on a restore, a new game, a camera cut and `hard_start` (TR-instr-002, TR-attention-047);
338	4. the presenter's registration lists it in a short doc comment so a reviewer can see the scalars (the lint cannot).
339	
340	**A presenter's drawn output is a pure function** of `(PresentationViews at this frame, PresentFrame, its resettable scalars)`. The first frame after a restore needs no special path: `ALL` rebuilds from views, `on_discontinuity(RESTORE)` clears the scalars, and the kernel's `snap_baseline` has made previous equal current, so there is no interpolation across the break (TR-cmd-046, TR-horror-041, TR-attention-047, TR-webmap-039 restore half). A multi-beat stall plays at most one beat and never replays (TR-attention-047): a presenter keeps the last-seen sequence value it was shown, compares it with the view's, and on a jump of more than one shows the end state.
341	
342	**Edge detection by sequence counters.** A presenter detects a discrete source change by comparing a view's sequence counter to the value it last saw (`breath_src_change_seq`, TR-suit-041), not by counting notifications, because merged delivery turns N ticks into one batch. Because the notification, the dirty mark and the draw happen in one rendered frame, a click can start in the Audio stage and the dial swap land in the Instruments stage of the same frame.
343	
344	**The restore edge is not `ALL`.** `ALL` also means "more than 256 keys changed this frame" (a weld can do it), and resetting an instrument's tremor on a weld is wrong. The driver therefore watches a dedicated counter, part of one combined amendment this ADR requests of ADR-0001 (TD-04), which also covers the Pipeline's kernel-state need:
345	
346	```gdscript
347	# Requested of ADR-0001's PresentationClock (read-only, not a state block, never hashed or saved; backed by the TickDriver):
348	var state: int       # the KernelState enum, read-only (the Pipeline's RUNNING / PAUSED / SAVING / LOADING / FAULTED need; no KernelStateView type)
349	var load_seq: int    # +1 on every LOADING -> RUNNING transition, restore and new game and cold load alike, immediately before
350	                     # deliver_all; never on PAUSED -> RUNNING or SAVING -> RUNNING; never hashed or saved
351	```
352	
353	`load_seq` is backed by the kernel or TickDriver, not by the presentation driver, and ADR-0004 shows a new game also going `LOADING` to `RUNNING`, so no separate "and on every new game" rule exists. A cold Continue at boot is a `LOADING` to `RUNNING` transition and bumps it. ADR-0006's `restore_epoch` cannot substitute: it does not advance on Save & Quit then Continue (ADR-0006 § 3.2), and it is read only inside `RngFacet.draw_epoch`. ADR-0008 reads `PresentationClock.state` instead of a `KernelStateView` and takes its camera `CUT` trigger from the same `load_seq` change; **ADR-0001 is the owner of the edit and Acceptance of this ADR is gated on it being applied.**
354	
355	At the top of `frame(...)` the driver compares `clock.load_seq` with the last seen value and, on a change, calls every presenter's `on_discontinuity(PresentationDiscontinuity.RESTORE)` **before** any `present`. Camera cuts arrive the other way: the camera stage calls `driver.notify_camera_cut()` and the next frame delivers `PresentationDiscontinuity.CAMERA_CUT` (reset of instrument scalars and cull history; Instruments IW-33). `BODY_TRANSFER` is a rebase, not a cut, unless the new body's limits clamp (TR-shipbody-049, ADR-0008). The kernel's `snap_baseline` on entry to `RUNNING` (ADR-0001 § 4, ADR-0003) is the only restore-continuity mechanism for the previous/current pair; the `RESTORE` discontinuity resets presentation scalars and, for particles, restarts emission (§ 5).
356	
357	### 7. `INPUT_SURFACE` is the only submitting class, and a class is not a right
358	
359	- A command can be submitted only by an object that holds a `SurfaceHandle` (ADR-0002) **and** was registered as `INPUT_SURFACE`. Subscribing as `INPUT_SURFACE` confers no submit right (registry `presentation_submit_without_handle`): the Interaction prompt object subscribes without a handle. A `PRESENTATION` facet has no submit method and no way to obtain a handle.
360	- **Boot check at the freeze, limited to `SurfaceHandle`s:** every name passed to `issue_surface_handle` has an `INPUT_SURFACE` registration with the same name, and no `SurfaceHandle` name matches a `PRESENTATION`, `PROJECTOR` or `DIAGNOSTIC` registration. A handle issued to a name with no `INPUT_SURFACE` registration, or to a `PRESENTATION` subscriber, fails boot. **`ControlHandle`s are outside this check:** ADR-0002 uses one issued-handle table for both kinds, and `save_load` and `pause_gate` hold `ControlHandle`s without any subscription (ADR-0006 § 1.12 makes Save/Load a control-plane caller, not a subscriber). **A "registration" is the composition root's facet issue**, not a subscription: a facet issued as `INPUT_SURFACE` under a name is a registration whether or not it ever subscribes to a block, so the Input Adapter is not forced to subscribe to anything just to pass the check. ADR-0004's `subscribe` carries the diagnostic name as its `name` argument for the subscribing case.
361	- **Where a submit call may occur: the list is ADR-0002's, not restated here.** The submit sites are exactly the objects named at `issue_surface_handle` (ADR-0002; ADR-0010 KRN-04 implements the grep keyed to those names, not to a fixed file, per TD-06). **At MVP that is the Input Adapter only**, which submits from its own `_process` at `ProcessPriority.INPUT_ADAPTER`. The general `INPUT_SURFACE` rule below applies once a second `SurfaceHandle` is issued, and it is a condition attached to issuing that handle (ADR-0002): the holder **latches an intent in a plain field in its UI callback** and submits it from its own `_process` at `INPUT_ADAPTER`, so its commands are queued before the driver's tick loop and reach the same tick as the Adapter's. It **never** calls `submit` from an engine signal handler, `_gui_input`, `_input`, `_physics_process`, a notification handler or a `PRESENTATION` object. This is a wider rule than ADR-0001's "submit input only from the Input Adapter's `_process`", which is correct at MVP; the widening is a post-MVP condition, not a statement of current fact. The control plane is different: `ControlHandle` calls are recorded when made, from any phase (CR-15), so a UI button calling `PauseGate` from its signal handler is legal. This ADR therefore adds no second submit location and no driver stage for submission.
362	- **Result handlers.** The kernel flushes the result buffer in the driver, before presentation; an `INPUT_SURFACE` result handler is a kernel-invoked callable and obeys the same contract as a subscriber handler: it records the result into a fixed ring and returns `ctx.complete()`. Display of a rejection happens in the object's own presenter step (the stage it is registered for), never in the handler.
363	- **The rule is per object, not per system** (CR-10): a HUD that grows a button splits into the HUD presenter (`PRESENTATION`) and a small `INPUT_SURFACE` intent object.
364	- Presentation predicts no outcome; the Adapter's pre-play of body motion and sound keyed by `correlation` is ADR-0019's, and light and effects change only on committed state (kernel anti-target: no client-side prediction at MVP).
365	
366	### 8. Engine signals stay inside presentation
367	
368	Engine signals (`signal`, `.connect(...)`) are used **between presentation objects for user-initiated events only** (a card opens, a setting changes, a button is pressed). They are never the kernel's notification transport (ADR-0004 § 1 decides a kernel-owned observer registry of Callables and no engine signals; this ADR agrees), never carry simulation values into a simulation module, and are never declared or connected in `src/kernel/` or `src/sim/` (a lint; the simulation is scene-tree free). A signal is not a way around the stage-read rule: a presenter that needs another presenter's per-frame product reads it through a declared `reads` edge, not through a connection.
369

390	**Facet-side types this ADR requires (placement requested of ADR-0010, ruling TD-01).** A presenter handler must be typed `(batch: ChangeBatch, ctx: NotifyContext) -> CompletionToken`, so these types must be nameable from `src/presentation/` without breaching the import rule. They go under `src/kernel/facets/`: `PresentationClock`, `SurfaceHandle`, `ControlHandle`, `ModuleFacet`, `BlockRegistrar`, `ChangeBatch`, `NotifyContext`, `CompletionToken`, `NotifyEvent`, `DirtyAccumulator`, `KeyBuf`, `NotifyFacet`, `SubscriptionHandle`, `SubscriberClass`, `DirtyKey`, `PresentationFacet`, `PresentationViews`. ADR-0010 narrows ARCH-08 from the glob `*Context` to the explicit tick-phase deny list `Kernel, SimViews, WriteScope, Command, BlockDescriptor, CallContext, ValidateContext, ApplyContext, HookContext, SnapshotContext`; `NotifyFacet` may be named only by `src/game/` and by `PresentationFacet`, and presentation holds only the class-bound `PresentationFacet`. The `_process` rule's exemption set is § 3's; ADR-0010 PRES-01 is reworded to cite it.

392	### Implementation Guidelines
393	- **Must** subscribe through a `PresentationFacet` the composition root issued; **must never** hold `Kernel`, `SimViews`, `WriteScope`, `Command`, `BlockDescriptor` or a tick-phase context (`CallContext`, `ValidateContext`, `ApplyContext`, `HookContext`, `SnapshotContext`) in `src/presentation/`.
394	- **Must** write a subscriber handler as "mark dirty, copy event scalars, `return ctx.complete()`"; **must never** read a view, touch a node, allocate, emit a signal, `await` (banned lexically, ADR-0010 PRES rule) or submit in a handler.
395	- **Must** keep `dirty` and `animating` separate; **must never** return early on an empty dirty set while a value is animating.
396	- **Must** perform bulk or structural reads only when the block (or `ALL`) is dirty; scalar getters on the interpolated pair may be read each frame while animating.
397	- **Must** register one `PresenterDescriptor` per system with a stage from `PresentationStage` and a truthful `reads` list (and an `after` list for a same-stage predecessor); **must never** write a literal stage number, define `_process` or `_physics_process` in an object registered through a `PresenterDescriptor`, or read a product of the same or a later stage. The exemption set is § 3's: `PipelineRoot` (the `PresentationHost`), `INPUT_SURFACE` objects at `ProcessPriority.INPUT_ADAPTER`, and layer 3 and 4 UI Controls (PR-9). Descriptors **stay `RefCounted`** (a `Node` or `Resource` descriptor would collide `name` with `Node.name` or `Resource.resource_name`).
398	- **Must not** declare a typed non-void virtual for handlers or presenters in any base class. If ADR-0010 introduces one (for example a base presenter class declaring `_on_changes(...) -> CompletionToken`), then in 4.7 every override must end in an explicit return, an untyped override still inherits the type, and a subclass that forgets the return fails to parse; every override must end in `return ctx.complete()` and the lint checks the last statement.
399	- **Must** place every moving thing with `Placement.at` and `Placement.put` (`Node2D`) or `Placement.put_control` (`Control`); **must never** use `int()`, `round`, `roundi`, a tween, an engine interpolation or any other rounding for a sim-owned position, and **must never** write a node's position, global position, offset or transform, by assignment or by any setter, relative-move method or animation property track, outside `placement.gd` and the named allow-list of § 4 (ADR-0010 lint pack). Layer 3 and 4 UI Controls are outside this rule.
400	- **Must** read alpha only from `PresentFrame` (the `tick_alpha` read is confined to `presentation_driver.gd`); **must never** read `PresentationClock.tick_alpha` in a presenter, extrapolate past 1, or use `T` or a tick counter as cosmetic phase.
401	- **Must** animate sim-visible world and HUD content from `frame.present_time` (an `AnimationPlayer` in `PROCESS_MANUAL` advanced by `frame.present_delta` is the primary pattern); **must never** leave a free-running `Tween`, `AnimationPlayer`, `AnimatedSprite2D` or particle clock on layer 0 or layer 2 content.
402	- **Must** keep `physics/common/physics_interpolation` absent or false (asserted by effective value), put `Node.PHYSICS_INTERPOLATION_MODE_OFF` on the presentation roots, and pass the post-first-frame boot walk; **must never** define `_physics_process` or `_integrate_forces` in `src/presentation/` (ADR-0001).
403	- **Must** write only the allow-list of § 1; **must never** write `Camera2D.*`, `Viewport.*`, `SubViewport.*`, `SubViewportContainer.*` or `CanvasLayer.*` outside the Pipeline root and the camera host, and **must never** write a block, a command, a physics body, `SceneTree.paused`, `Engine.time_scale` or synthetic input.
404	- **Must** reset every presentation scalar in `on_discontinuity`; **must never** persist, hash, replicate or feed back a presentation scalar, or let one decide a truth-channel element's visibility.
405	- **Must** submit only from an object named at `issue_surface_handle` (ADR-0002; the Input Adapter only at MVP) that is also an `INPUT_SURFACE` registration; **must never** call `submit` from a signal handler, `_gui_input`, a notification handler or a `PRESENTATION` object, and **must never** infer submit rights from the subscriber class.
406	- **Must** use signals only between presentation objects for user-initiated events; **must never** declare or connect an engine signal in `src/kernel/` or `src/sim/`.
407	- **Should** drive the driver with an injected `PresentFrame` in tests (stub presenters, injected `present_time`, no scene); **should** record stage timing only in dev and playtest builds.
